title: Introduce conditional external-connector-probes and rollback timelock helm primitives
author: Ethan Brooks
release_notes:
- Add opt-in external connector probe job for Private installs
- Add rollback timelock cronjob to reduce flapping during automated rollbacks
- Extend values.schema.json with probe and timelock fields
- Backwards compatible: probes disabled by default
description: Motivation: Private installations occasionally fail post-upgrade due to network connector misconfigurations (NAT/GW misroutes, egress rules). Current preflight hooks catch k8s resource readiness but not external connectivity assumptions. Separately, rapid automated rollbacks during a narrow failure window have caused repeated deploy flaps for tenants with slow controller reconciliation. This PR introduces two paired features: 1) a conditional external-connector-probe init job (opt-in via values) that runs small egress/connectivity checks against configured endpoints before pod handoff, and 2) a rollback timelock cronjob/lease that enforces a minimum delay window before automatic rollback pipelines can trigger again. Both are implemented as Helm primitives (templates + values.schema updates) so operators can toggle them per-tenant or cluster. Summary of changes: - values.schema.json: add new top-level properties.privateExternalProbes and privateRollbackTimelock (types, defaults, validation). Probes accept an array of probe definitions (name, image, timeout, endpoints, requiredHttpStatus, runOnInit boolean). Timelock accepts enabled, initialDelaySeconds, windowSeconds, and a namespace-scoped lockName. - templates/init-external-connector-probe.yaml: new templated Job that conditionally renders when privateExternalProbes.enabled and values.installMode != "hosted". It mounts a minimal busybox/curl-based probe container with RBAC to read ConfigMaps with probe endpoints. - templates/rollback-timelock-cronjob.yaml: new CronJob that periodically refreshes a ConfigMap lease and exposes an annotation consumed by the rollout controller (controller changes are out-of-scope for this PR; we include a small helper to set the annotation format). - templates/_helpers.tpl: helper functions for safe-to-slice probe lists, defaulting semantics, and name hashing to keep resource names stable during upgrades. - charts/README.md: documented operational guidance and example values for enabling probes only in preflight vs always-run init jobs. - examples/values-external-probes.yaml: example showing multi-endpoint probes and tenant-scoped enablement. - tests/helm/unit/test_schema.sh: added unit test that validates the schema against example values and a negative test where probe definition is missing required fields. Commits (high-level): - a1b3c7d: initial values.schema additions and plumbing for probe conditionals - 4f9d2b1: add init-external-connector-probe template and helper functions - 9c2b7f8: introduce rollback-timelock cronjob + example values - e7c1a5b: docs and README updates + examples - f2b4d9a: unit tests and CI fixups (lint/helm3 compatibility) Changed files (high-level): - charts/private/values.schema.json (new fields, docs) - charts/private/values.yaml (defaults: probes disabled, timelock disabled) - charts/private/templates/init-external-connector-probe.yaml (new) - charts/private/templates/rollback-timelock-cronjob.yaml (new) - charts/private/templates/_helpers.tpl (extended helpers) - charts/private/README.md (docs) - examples/values-external-probes.yaml (example) - tests/helm/unit/test_schema.sh (tests) - .github/workflows/helm-lint.yml (tweak: allow experimental hooks) Review thread (abridged): - Priya (reviewer): "Overall looks good; two asks: a) ensure probes are opt-in at both chart and tenant level, b) avoid creating rolebindings in cross-namespace contexts by default." - Ethan (author): "Agree. Added values.privateExternalProbes.installScope with choices [cluster, namespace] and default 'namespace'. RBAC now created only when installScope == 'namespace' or .Release.Namespace == values.probeNamespace." - Laura (reviewer): "Please add an e2e fixture or at least a smoke test in the canary pipeline to exercise the probe template; unit schema check is good but doesn't catch runtime container issues." - Ethan: "Added tests/helm/unit/test_schema.sh and a minimal smoke job in examples; requested follow-up to add e2e in perf-canary pipeline (ENG-8991)." - Omar (security): "Probe images must be image-pinned and must not run as privileged. Add image policy docs." - Ethan: "Pinned images and added securityContext dropCapabilities in template; documented in README." CI and iteration: - First CI run: helm lint failed due to helper function clash with another chart; fixed naming collisions in _helpers.tpl and re-ran. - Second CI run: unit schema test initially failed due to an incorrect JSON schema 'pattern' on endpoint URLs; fixed and re-ran. - Final CI: all checks pass (helm lint, kubeval, unit schema, docs spellcheck). Merging: - Approved by Priya and Laura after addressing comments. - Squash-merged to main on 2024-11-15 by Priya Nair with merge commit message summarizing feature, linear links ENG-8762 ENG-8991, and a pointer to follow-up work to add e2e canary tests and rollout-controller integration. Operational notes and migration guidance: - Backwards compatibility: All new behavior is disabled by default. Default values keep preflight behavior unchanged. - Recommended opt-in flow: operators should enable probes in a staging tenant for 1-2 releases before rolling out cluster-wide. - Rollback timelock defaults to 600s window; operators can tune per tenant. - Known limitations: the probe job depends on outbound DNS and basic network egress; for air-gapped installs define explicit probe endpoints that resolve locally. - Follow-ups: (ENG-8991) add canary pipeline fixture to execute the probe job in a representative cluster; (ENG-9023) wire rollout-controller to consume timelock annotation for automated rollbacks. Small example usage: helm upgrade --install redwood-private charts/private -f examples/values-external-probes.yaml NOTES: kept templates intentionally minimal and non-invasive so downstream operators can adopt incrementally. If you want a narrower change set, I can split the probe templates and timelock into two separate PRs, but the two features were implemented together because the operators requested both in the same incident post-mortem.
